Reportedly, Apple surpassed $10 billion in annual sales in India for the first time in the previous fiscal year.

Achieving such a figure in a country where the average annual income is under $3,000 is particularly remarkable—especially considering iPhones are priced higher in India than in the U.S…

For years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. But in recent years, with local economic growth and the company finally being able to open Apple Stores in the country, the situation has changed dramatically.

Bloomberg reported the latest milestone today.

Given the low local per capita income and that iPhones are manufactured in India, you might expect the prices to be far lower than in the U.S. In fact, however, high taxes have made Apple products more expensive in India than in the U.S.

Apple has tried to offset this issue to some extent by partnering with banks to offer credit card cashback.

About a quarter of iPhones are now made in India, though most are shipped to the U.S. for sale. Apple restructured its logistics arrangements to avoid the U.S. tariffs imposed on Chinese imports.
